michael_schumacher.name: Michael Schumacher
michael_schumacher.about: Seven world titles and 91 wins built on relentless preparation. Schumacher rebuilt Ferrari around himself, turning a sleeping giant into the most dominant force of the early 2000s. Ruthless in wheel-to-wheel combat, untouchable in the wet, and the benchmark every driver since has been measured against.

ayrton_senna.name: Ayrton Senna
ayrton_senna.about: The purest qualifying pace the sport has ever seen — 65 poles, many of them on laps he described in almost spiritual terms. Senna drove on instinct and conviction, refused to yield an inch, and remains the emotional heart of Formula 1 three decades after Imola.

alain_prost.name: Alain Prost
alain_prost.about: Four titles won by thinking, not thrashing. Prost managed fuel, tyres and risk better than anyone of his era, routinely winning races he had no business winning by simply being the last man with something left. The intellectual counterweight to Senna's fire.

nico_rosberg.name: Nico Rosberg
nico_rosberg.about: Beat Lewis Hamilton over a season by out-preparing him — obsessive data work, engineer relationships and mental margins rather than raw speed. Won the 2016 title and retired five days later, having decided there was nothing left to prove.

daniel_ricciardo.name: Daniel Ricciardo
daniel_ricciardo.about: The best late-braker of his generation and the widest smile on the grid. Ricciardo built a career on audacious lunges from impossible distances back — Monaco, Monza, Shanghai — and made the shoey a global celebration.

sebastian_vettel.name: Sebastian Vettel
sebastian_vettel.about: Four straight titles from 2010 to 2013, built on ruthless qualifying pace and a Red Bull car Adrian Newey sculpted around him. The most emotionally open of his generation's dominant champions — tears at his final race, hugs for the mechanics, and a growing conscience that outlasted his time on track.

kimi_raikkonen.name: Kimi Räikkönen
kimi_raikkonen.about: Deadpan on the radio, ruthless on track. Räikkönen won his only title in 2007 by a single point, then spent fourteen more years proving speed doesn't need a personality attached to it — "leave me alone, I know what I'm doing" remains the most Kimi sentence ever broadcast.

nigel_mansell.name: Nigel Mansell
nigel_mansell.about: Ferocious, fan-adored, and never once boring. Mansell's 1992 season in the dominant Williams FW14B — nine wins from sixteen races — remains one of the most one-sided title runs in history, the payoff for a career built on wheel-to-wheel combat and a refusal to lift.

niki_lauda.name: Niki Lauda
niki_lauda.about: Survived a fireball at the Nürburgring in 1976, was read his last rites, and was back in the cockpit six weeks later with his burns still raw. Then, a year on, calmly withdrew from the title-deciding Japanese GP in torrential rain, deciding the points weren't worth the risk. The only driver ever to win championships with both Ferrari and McLaren.
